newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 2.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* Data showed the U.S. economy has accelerated in recent weeks although inflation seemed to remain constrained.
* Chrysler high-profit light truck sales fell two-tenths of one percent last month compared to March 1996.
* Bre-X Minerals shares rose after a selloff prompted by controversy surrounding the company's gold find in Indonesia.
* The stock market recovered slightly after a two-day fall. The Dow Industrials closed up 27.57 at 6,611.05.
* Informix shares sank as the company said it expected to reported a first quarter loss due to weak sales.
* Market place: Analysts say Triarc has some advantages which might help it succeed with its newly-acquired brand Snapple.
* Big car rental companies have stopped letting people rent cars using just debt cards from Visa or Mastercard.
* An administrative law judge ruled a hospital owned by Columbia/HCA in Kentucky violated Federal labor laws.
* A warning from Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin about Japan's trade surplus caused the dollar to fall.
* The U.S. Agriculture Department said it previously overstated soybean stockpiles, an announcement which caused soybean prices to rise.
* Dow Chemical filed a suit against General Electric charging the company "aggressively" hired Dow employees who had access to trade secrets.
* Japan announced plans to rescue two of the country's biggest banks and have them withdraw from international business.
* In June, Kazuo Inamori plans to retire as head of Japan's Kyocera and DDI, to indulge an interest in religion.
* Advertising: Schieffelin & Somerset has a new line of ads for Tanqueray vodka.
* Hong Kong hotels are moving quickly to add technology to hotel rooms to please businessmen.
